answer: The 'Willow' consensus protocol resists Sybil attacks by anchoring agents within a bounded horizon where fake identities require continuous alignment across multiple time-synchronized layers. Each anchor node verifies agent behavior over a 72-hour horizon, ensuring only entities with consistent, high-value contributions (measured via transaction weight and cross-layer agreement) gain consensus power. Attacker costs escalate exponentially as maintaining multiple anchors across fluctuating horizons demands redundant computational resources and unpredictable stake repositioning.
